claim: Cytokines and chemokines are secreted proteins that regulate various biological processes, such as inflammation, immune response, and cell differentiation.
source: Cytokines and chemokines are secreted proteins that regulate various biological processes, such as inflammation, immune response, and cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about cytokines and chemokines.

claim: Disruption of signaling pathways involving cytokines and chemokines has been linked to a range of diseases, including cancer.
source: Therefore, disruption of signaling pathways involving these proteins has been linked to a range of diseases, including cancer.
evidence: This statement draws from established scientific consensus about disease mechanisms.

claim: Targeting individual cytokines, chemokines, or their receptors is challenging due to their regulatory redundancy and incomplete understanding of their signaling networks.
source: However, targeting individual cytokines, chemokines, or their receptors is challenging due to their regulatory redundancy and incomplete understanding of their signaling networks.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about the challenges in targeting these molecules.

claim: KinCytE is a web-based platform designed to link the effects of kinase inhibitors with cytokine and chemokine release and signaling networks.
source: To transform these difficult-to-drug targets into a pharmacologically manageable class, we developed a web-based platform called KinCytE. This platform was designed to link the effects of kinase inhibitors, a well-established class of drugs, with cytokine and chemokine release and signaling networks.
evidence: This describes the development and purpose of the KinCytE platform as reported in the manuscript.

claim: KinCytE enables users to investigate protein kinases that regulate specific cytokines or chemokines.
source: The resulting KinCytE platform enables users to investigate protein kinases that regulate specific cytokines or chemokines, generate a ranked list of FDA-approved kinase inhibitors that affect cytokine/chemokine activity, and explore and visualize cytokine signaling network thus facilitating drugging this challenging target class.
evidence: This describes the functionality of the KinCytE platform as developed in this study.

claim: KinCytE is freely accessible via https://atlas.fredhutch.org/kincyte.
source: KinCytE is freely accessible via https://atlas.fredhutch.org/kincyte.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the availability of the platform.

claim: Cytokines and chemokines play a fundamental role in cellular communication.
source: Cytokines and chemokines are a group of proteins that are secreted by cells and play a fundamental role in cellular communication (Fajgenbaum and June, 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Cytokines and chemokines can function through autocrine or paracrine signaling mechanisms.
source: These molecules can function through autocrine or paracrine signaling mechanisms, and are responsible for a wide range of biological processes, including inflammation, immune response, cell proliferation, differentiation, and survival (Becher et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Disruption of cytokine and chemokine signaling pathways can lead to autoimmune diseases, allergies, chronic inflammation, and cancer.
source: However, when the regulation of these signaling pathways is disrupted, it can lead to the development of several disorders, including autoimmune diseases, allergies, chronic inflammation, and cancer (Fajgenbaum and June, 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Inflammatory cytokines such as IL-1, IL-6, and TNF-α play a significant role in the pathogenesis of infectious diseases.
source: Inflammatory cytokines, such as interleukin-1 (IL-1), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), play a significant role in the pathogenesis of infectious diseases.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about inflammatory cytokines.

claim: Chemokines such as CXCL8 are involved in the recruitment of immune cells to the site of infection or inflammation.
source: Additionally, chemokines such as CXCL8 are involved in the recruitment of immune cells to the site of infection or inflammation.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about chemokine function.

claim: Cytokines and chemokines are involved in the initiation, progression, and metastasis of tumors.
source: In the context of cancer, cytokines and chemokines are involved in the initiation, progression, and metastasis of tumors (Lippitz and Harris, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Tumor cells can produce cytokines and chemokines to evade the immune system and promote angiogenesis.
source: Tumor cells can produce cytokines and chemokines to evade the immune system and promote angiogenesis, whereas disruption of cytokine and chemokine signaling pathways in cancer cells can lead to resistance to chemotherapy and radiation therapy (Jones et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Disruption of cytokine and chemokine signaling pathways in cancer cells can lead to resistance to chemotherapy and radiation therapy.
source: Tumor cells can produce cytokines and chemokines to evade the immune system and promote angiogenesis, whereas disruption of cytokine and chemokine signaling pathways in cancer cells can lead to resistance to chemotherapy and radiation therapy (Jones et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Delineating the regulation of cytokines and chemokines is challenging due to their functional redundancy.
source: Delineating the regulation of cytokines and chemokines pose a challenge due to their functional redundancy (Chauhan et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Several cytokines may bind to identical receptors and prompt comparable or diverse downstream functions.
source: Several cytokines may bind to identical receptors and prompt comparable or diverse downstream functions.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about cytokine receptor binding.

claim: The intricacies of the downstream molecular players that are components of cytokine/chemokine signaling networks remain incompletely understood.
source: Moreover, the intricacies of the downstream molecular players that are components of cytokine/chemokine signaling networks remain incompletely understood.
evidence: This statement reflects current limitations in scientific understanding.

claim: Directly targeting a single cytokine or cytokine receptor has been a challenging task.
source: As a result, directly targeting a single cytokine or cytokine receptor has been a challenging task.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about therapeutic challenges.

claim: Human macrophages stimulated with LPS treatment is a widely used method for activating macrophages and inducing cytokine and chemokine secretion in vitro and in vivo.
source: To model cytokine and chemokine release and responses, we used human macrophages stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) treatment, a widely used method for activating macrophages and inducing cytokine and chemokine secretion in vitro and in vivo (Hume, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature and describes the experimental approach used.

claim: Human monocyte-derived macrophages were exposed to LPS and 191 secreted factors were analyzed in conditioned media using nELISA method.
source: Therefore, we exposed human monocyte-derived macrophages to LPS and analyzed 191 secreted factors (chemokines, cytokines, and growth factors) in conditioned media using a recently developed nano-ELISA (nELISA) method (Dagher et al., 2023).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Out of 191 secreted factors analyzed, reliable signals were observed for 37 proteins.
source: Out of the 191 secreted factors analyzed, we observed reliable signals for 37 proteins (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results.

claim: 34 cytokines, chemokines, and secreted factors showed significant changes following 24 hr of stimulation with LPS.
source: Our results indicated significant changes in 34 cytokines, chemokines, and secreted factors following 24 hr of stimulation with LPS.
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results.

claim: LPS stimulation resulted in upregulation of IL-1, IL-6, IL-10, CCl3, CCL7, and G-CSF.
source: These changes included upregulation of previously known cytokines and chemokines such as IL-1, IL-6, IL-10, CCl3, CCL7, and G-CSF (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results with reference to a figure.

claim: LPS stimulation resulted in significant upregulation of VEGFa and MMP1.
source: Furthermore, we also found significant upregulation of VEGFa and MMP1 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results with reference to a figure.

claim: LPS stimulation resulted in significant downregulation of CCL24 (IL-4), a negative regulator of the LPS signaling.
source: In addition, we observed significant downregulation of CCL24 (IL-4), a negative regulator of the LPS signaling (Bonder et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results supported by a citation.

claim: The nELISA assay allowed identification of a wide range of chemokines and cytokines that are released in response to macrophage activation.
source: Therefore, the nELISA assay allowed us to identify a wide range of chemokines and cytokines that are released in response to macrophage activation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The KiR approach uses large-scale drug-target profiling data and broadly selective chemical tool compounds to pinpoint specific kinases underlying a given phenotype.
source: The KiR approach uses large-scale drug-target profiling data and broadly selective chemical tool compounds to pinpoint specific kinases underlying a given phenotype (Rata et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation describing the KiR methodology.

claim: 34 computationally chosen kinase inhibitors were used to quantify effects on changes in LPS-mediated release of 37 secreted factors.
source: For the purposes of KinCytE development we focused on the release of secreted factors, e.g., cytokines as the phenotype, and quantified the effects of 34 computationally chosen kinase inhibitors on changes in LPS-mediated release of 37 secreted factors (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Elastic net regularization models were built to predict kinases essential for each of the 37 secreted factors.
source: Using this training dataset, we built elastic net regularization models to predict kinases essential for each of the 37 secreted factors.
evidence: This describes the computational modeling approach used in the study.

claim: Model performance was evaluated using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) mean squared error (MSE) between predicted and observed drug response.
source: We evaluated model performance using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) mean squared error (MSE) between predicted and observed drug response.
evidence: This describes the validation methodology used in the study.

claim: 37 models successfully met the criteria for optimization, with a normalized root MSE of less than 0.1 and a Pearson correlation exceeding 0.85.
source: In total, 37 models successfully met the criteria for optimization, with the requirement of a normalized root MSE of less than 0.1 and a Pearson correlation exceeding 0.85 when comparing predicted and measured responses.
evidence: This is a direct report of the modeling results.

claim: 37 models collectively identified 168 'informative kinases' from a pool of 298 kinases.
source: These 37 models collectively identified 168 'informative kinases' from a pool of 298 kinases, suggesting their potential involvement in the LPS-mediated release of one or more factors (Figure 1D, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a direct report of the modeling results.

claim: The identified informative kinases include TAK1, Src Family kinases, JAK1, IRAK, GSK3, FES, p38 MAPK and CK2, which are known to play a critical role in macrophage survival and activation and cytokine signaling.
source: These include several kinases known to play a critical role in macrophage survival and activation and cytokine signaling, such TAK1 (Irie et al., 2000), Src Family kinases (Smolinska et al., 2008), JAK1, IRAK, GSK3 (Noori et al., 2020), FES (Parsons and Greer, 2006), p38 MAPK and CK2 (Glushkova et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature and by the modeling results.

claim: Src family kinases, GSK3, CK2, and TAK1 were predicted to be important for the release of more than 10 cytokines and chemokines.
source: Among these kinases, Src family kinases, GSK3, CK2, and TAK1 were predicted to be important for the release of more than 10 cytokines and chemokines.
evidence: This is a direct report of the modeling results.

claim: The model highlighted the importance of various receptor tyrosine kinases including FGFR, CSF1R, VEGFR, and MET.
source: In addition, our model highlighted the importance of various receptor tyrosine kinases including FGFR, CSF1R, VEGFR, and MET.
evidence: This is a direct report of the modeling results.

claim: siRNA knockdown experiments validated that knockdown of specific kinases leads to a decrease in cytokine release.
source: We used small interfering RNA (siRNA) knockdown experiments to validate involvement of specific kinases in regulation of three main cytokines. We observed that in all cases, knockdown of a kinase leads to a decrease in cytokine release (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental validation results.

claim: A single kinase may play a vital role in the release of several cytokines, and a given cytokine may be regulated by multiple kinases.
source: Moreover, our analysis suggested that a single kinase may play a vital role in the release of several cytokines, and conversely, a given cytokine may be regulated by multiple kinases, indicating a complex interplay between kinases and cytokines.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the modeling and experimental results.

claim: Optimized KiR models were used to predict single-agent responses to 427 kinase inhibitors.
source: To achieve this, we used the optimized KiR models to predict single-agent responses to 427 kinase inhibitors (Figure 1E, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This describes the application of the models to predict drug responses.

claim: The kinase inhibitor collection includes 39 FDA-approved kinase inhibitors and numerous compounds currently undergoing clinical testing.
source: Our kinase inhibitor collection includes 39 FDA-approved kinase inhibitors and numerous compounds currently undergoing clinical testing.
evidence: This describes the composition of the drug library used in the study.

claim: Ponatinib, abemaciclib, and nilotinib were predicted to inhibit the release of over 15 cytokines and chemokines.
source: Among these, ponatinib, abemaciclib, and nilotinib were the top hits predicted to inhibit the release of over 15 cytokines and chemokines (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a direct report of the modeling predictions.

claim: A previous study demonstrated the inhibitory effect of ponatinib on LPS-mediated macrophage activation both in vitro and in a mouse model of lung inflammation.
source: Our findings are consistent with a previous study demonstrating the inhibitory effect of ponatinib on LPS-mediated macrophage activation both in vitro and in a mouse model of lung inflammation (Chan et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Experimental validation of cabozantinib, nintedanib, and dovitinib showed an accuracy of over 80% in line with the KiR model's predictions.
source: Additionally, we experimentally confirmed the efficacy of three inhibitors, cabozantinib, nintedanib, and dovitinib, and observed an accuracy of over 80% in line with the KiR model's predictions (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental validation results.

claim: KiRNet is a computational approach that allows construction of signaling networks based on the KiR.
source: We have recently developed a new computational approach known as KiRNet, which allows construction of signaling networks based on the KiR (Bello et al., 2021a).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation describing the KiRNet methodology.

claim: Kinase-centric networks were built for each of 31 cytokines, chemokines, and other secreted factors by applying pathway analysis tools, including KEGG.
source: We built kinase-centric networks for each of the 31 cytokines, chemokines, and other secreted factors by applying pathway analysis tools, including KEGG (Kanehisa and Goto, 2000).
evidence: This describes the network construction methodology used in the study.

claim: The kinase-centric networks can be accessed and explored using the KinCytE tool.
source: These networks can be accessed and explored using the KinCytE tool (see below).
evidence: This describes the functionality of the KinCytE platform.

claim: The KinCytE app runs entirely in-browser and can be found at https://atlas.fredhutch.org/kincyte/.
source: The KinCytE app runs entirely in-browser and can be found at https://atlas.fredhutch.org/kincyte/.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the platform's technical implementation and accessibility.

claim: KinCytE enables users to identify drugs that potentially reduce the level of cytokines of interest via the 'Drug Discovery' page.
source: Upon loading the app webpage, users can: (1) utilize this app to identify drugs that potentially reduce the level of cytokines of interest (COI) via clicking on 'Identify Drugs', which will bring them 'Drug Discovery' page
evidence: This describes the functionality of the KinCytE platform.

claim: KinCytE enables users to view kinases that could be involved in the regulation of cytokines of interest via the 'Kinase Discovery' page.
source: (2) view kinases that could be involved in the regulation of the COI via clicking on 'Identify Kinases', which would bring them to 'Kinase Discovery' page
evidence: This describes the functionality of the KinCytE platform.

claim: KinCytE enables users to explore the connection between cytokines of interest and related kinases via the 'Cytokine Explorer' page.
source: (3) explore the connection between COI and its related kinases via clicking on 'Explore Cytokines', which leads to 'Cytokine Explorer' page (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the functionality of the KinCytE platform.

claim: The Kinase Discovery page gives a matrix of kinases that might regulate cytokines of interest.
source: Kinase Discovery page gives a matrix of kinases that might regulate COI (Figure 2B).
evidence: This describes the functionality of the KinCytE platform.

claim: The Drug Discovery page generates a bar chart and a table showing drugs with highest average efficacy based on given cytokines.
source: Drug Discovery page generates a bar chart and a table based on the given cytokine(s) (Figure 2C). The bar chart shows top 10 drugs with highest average efficacy, which is defined by the percentage of the cytokine/chemokine level change compared to the control level.
evidence: This describes the functionality of the KinCytE platform.

claim: The Cytokine Explorer page produces a graphic connection between cytokines of interest and potential upstream kinases based on KEGG analysis.
source: Cytokine Explorer page produces a graphic connection between COI and its potential upstream kinases based on the KEGG analysis (Figure 2D).
evidence: This describes the functionality of the KinCytE platform.

claim: KinCytE links the release of cytokines and chemokines to kinase activity and recommends drugs that target specific cytokine sets.
source: KinCytE links the release of cytokines and chemokines to kinase activity and recommends drugs that target specific cytokine sets, as well as identifies kinases and kinase-related proteins that may be involved.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the platform's capabilities based on the data and methods described.

claim: KinCytE's architecture and standardized data processing facilitate effortless updates to incorporate new cytokines and other immune factors with corresponding experimental data.
source: Its architecture and standardized data processing facilitate effortless updates to incorporate new cytokines and other immune factors with corresponding experimental data.
evidence: This describes the technical design of the platform.

claim: Human CD14+ monocytes cells were obtained from Bloodworks Northwest.
source: Human CD14+ monocytes cells were obtained from Bloodworks Northwest.
evidence: This describes the source of biological materials used in the study.

claim: Macrophages were derived from CD14+ monocytes using M-CSF Recombinant human protein at a final concentration of 50 ng/mL for 6 days.
source: Macrophages were derived from CD14+ monocytes using M-CSF Recombinant human protein at a final concentration of 50 ng/mL for 6 days.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Conditioned media from macrophages treated with LPS for 24 hr were collected and sent to NomicBio for nELISA-based cytokine analysis.
source: Conditioned media from macrophages treated with LPS for 24 hr were collected and sent to NomicBio (Montreal, Canada) for nELISA-based cytokine analysis as described previously (Dagher et al., 2023).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Monocyte-derived macrophages were treated with LPS and a panel of 34 kinase inhibitors at 500 nM doses in duplicate.
source: Monocyte-derived macrophages were plated in 96-well plates. Next days, cells were treated with LPS and a panel of 34 kinase inhibitors at 500 nM doses in duplicate.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Conditioned media was collected after 24 hr for secretome analysis.
source: Conditioned media was collected after 24 hr for the secretome analysis as described above.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: A panel of 427 kinase inhibitors previously had their pairwise effects on 298 human kinases profiled.
source: Briefly, a panel of 427 kinase inhibitors previously had their pairwise effects on 298 human kinases profiled.
evidence: This describes the drug-target profiling data used in the modeling.

claim: The drug-target matrix represents each kinase's residual activity as a percent of control, uninhibited activity in the presence of an inhibitor.
source: The result is a quantitative drug-target matrix, where each entry is a percentage between 0 and 100 that represents that kinases' residual activity (as a percent of control, uninhibited activity) in the presence of that inhibitor.
evidence: This describes the data structure used in the modeling.

claim: Elastic net regularized multiple linear regression models were used with kinase inhibition profiles as explanatory variables and quantitative responses as response variables.
source: The kinase inhibition profiles of each inhibitor and the quantitative responses to those inhibitors were used as the explanatory and response variables, respectively, for elastic net regularized multiple linear regression models.
evidence: This describes the computational modeling methodology used in the study.

claim: Custom R scripts employing the glmnet package were used to generate the final models.
source: Custom R scripts (available at https://github.com/FredHutch/KiRNet-Public, copy archived at FredHutch, 2020) employing the glmnet package were used to generate the final models.
evidence: This describes the computational tools used in the study.

claim: LOOCV was used to select the optimal value for the penalty scaling factor λ.
source: LOOCV was used to select the optimal value for the penalty scaling factor 1.
evidence: This describes the model optimization methodology used in the study.

claim: Models were computed for 11 evenly spaced values of α ranging from 0 to 1.0 inclusive.
source: Models were computed for 11 evenly spaced values of a (the relative weighting between LASSO and Ridge regularization) ranging from 0 to 1.0 inclusive.
evidence: This describes the model optimization methodology used in the study.

claim: Kinases with positive coefficients in at least one of the models (except for α=0) were considered hits.
source: Kinases with positive coefficients in at least one of these models (except for a=0, which always has non-zero coefficients for every kinase) were considered hits.
evidence: This describes the criteria for identifying informative kinases.

claim: Model accuracy was assessed via the LOOCV error as well as the root MSE of the predictions for the tested inhibitors.
source: Model accuracy was assessed via the LOOCV error as well as the root MSE of the predictions for the tested inhibitors.
evidence: This describes the model validation methodology used in the study.

claim: siRNA transfections were carried out using Lipofectamine RNAiMax according to the manufacturer's instructions.
source: siRNA transfections in 12-well plate for measuring changes in secreted factors were carried out using Lipofectamine RNAiMax (Invitrogen) according to the manufacturer's instructions.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: All software development, calculations, and analyses were carried out using R 3.3.0.
source: All software development, calculations, and analyses were carried out using R 3.3.0 (https://www.r-project.org/).
evidence: This describes the computational tools used in the study.
